name: Projected Distinguishing Range / Projected Membership Queries Complexity
details: For every projection, querying a distinguishing coordinate set identifies its target.
proof: For each coordinate projection $\mathcal G=\mathcal H_{|S}$, query the target on a smallest coordinate set distinguishing all concepts of $\mathcal G$. The resulting trace identifies the target, hence $\mathrm Q_m(\mathcal G)\leq\mathrm R(\mathcal G)$. Taking maxima over projections gives $\mathrm Q_m^p(\mathcal H)\leq\mathrm R^p(\mathcal H).
witness_verification: For half-intervals, $\mathrm R^p=n-1$, while $\mathrm Q_m^p=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$. Hence the gap is unbounded.
